quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #2
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 35

questions.question: Which statement is true about medications and driving?

options.text: Most cold medications can make you drowsy.
Over-the-counter medicines are safe to drive with if you take the recommended dose.
Prescription medications are always safe to take while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Most cold medications can make you drowsy.
questions.explanation: All medications—prescription and over-the-counter—can be dangerous while driving. Cold and allergy medicines can make you drowsy and hurt your driving ability. You are responsible for knowing how your medications affect your driving.

questions.question: If you drive slower than the traffic around you, what will most likely happen?

options.text: You will block traffic and may get a ticket.
You will show good defensive driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will block traffic and may get a ticket.
questions.explanation: You should drive slowly in heavy traffic or bad weather. But if you drive too slowly and block traffic, you can get a ticket. Match the speed of other traffic unless the traffic is going over the speed limit.

questions.question: When turning left from a multilane one-way street to another one-way street, start from:

options.text: Any lane, as long as it is safe.

questions.explanation: When turning left from a one-way street onto another one-way street, you must start the turn from the leftmost lane.

questions.question: What does this sign warn you about?
questions.explanation: A round sign means a railroad crossing is ahead. This sign is posted a few hundred feet before the tracks. It tells you to slow down, look, listen, and get ready to stop.

questions.question: On a multilane road, what does a dashed yellow line next to a solid yellow line mean?

options.text: No one can pass from either direction.
Everyone can pass from both directions.
Only drivers next to the dashed line can pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only drivers next to the dashed line can pass.
questions.explanation: When yellow lines have both solid and dashed markings, only the traffic next to the dashed line can cross to pass. Drivers next to the solid line cannot pass.

questions.question: Which statement is true about alcohol and driving?

options.text: If you can walk straight, it is safe to drive.
If your blood alcohol is below the legal limit, driving is not impaired.
Alcohol affects your judgment, which you need to drive safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol affects your judgment, which you need to drive safely.
questions.explanation: Alcohol affects your judgment. You need good judgment to react to things on the road. Even small amounts of alcohol can hurt your ability to drive safely, even if you are below the legal limit.

questions.question: What is true about driving too fast?

options.text: It saves time so you reach your destination quicker.
It increases the risk of serious injury and death.

questions.correctAnswerText: It increases the risk of serious injury and death.
questions.explanation: Speeding is a major cause of crashes. It does not save time and often leads to dangerous decisions.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign tells you a steep hill is coming. Slow down and be ready to shift to a lower gear to control your speed and protect your brakes.

questions.question: When you see an octagonal sign, you must:
questions.explanation: An octagonal (eight-sided) sign always means "Stop." Come to a complete stop, give the right-of-way to traffic and pedestrians, and proceed when the road is clear.

questions.question: If there is no crosswalk and a pedestrian is crossing your lane, you should:

options.text: Make sure the pedestrian sees you before going.
Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.
questions.explanation: You must always give pedestrians the right-of-way, even without a marked crosswalk.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: A yellow triangle with black letters means no passing zone. You will see this sign on two-lane roads where you cannot pass other vehicles.

questions.question: Which statement about driving speed is true?

options.text: As your speed increases, the chance of a fatality increases.
As your speed increases, so should your following distance.

questions.explanation: Higher speeds increase the chance of death in a crash. At speeds above 80 mph, survival is unlikely. Higher speeds also increase stopping distance, so you need more space between you and other vehicles.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Reserved parking for persons with disabilities.

questions.explanation: This sign is posted where you cannot enter. You may see it on one-way streets or if you try to enter a highway ramp the wrong way.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Reserved parking for persons with disabilities.

questions.explanation: This sign warns that two lanes of traffic going the same direction will soon combine into one lane.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Right turns permitted on a red light.

questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn right. It is illegal to make a right turn where this sign is posted.

questions.question: This is the shape and color of a ____ sign.
questions.explanation: Triangle signs pointing down mean yield. Slow down when you see this sign and stop if needed. Stop at a marked line if one exists.

questions.question: This sign shows one type of:
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They tell you about conditions ahead. This sign warns that another road crosses the highway ahead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign tells you a traffic rule. You cannot make a right turn where this sign is posted.

questions.question: When passing parked vehicles, you should:

options.text: Be ready for a person or vehicle to suddenly move into your lane.
Expect all other drivers and pedestrians to respect your right-of-way.
Drive close to the parked vehicles to give more room to moving traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready for a person or vehicle to suddenly move into your lane.
questions.explanation: Keep distance from parked vehicles. A person may step out without looking. A driver may start moving their car before seeing you.

questions.question: When driving in work zones, you should:

options.text: Follow the driver in front of you closely.
Pass the driver in front of you as soon as you can.
Do not tailgate and keep a safe distance from other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not tailgate and keep a safe distance from other vehicles.
questions.explanation: In work zones, keep distance from barriers, trucks, equipment, workers, and other vehicles. Increase your following distance and do not tailgate.

questions.question: What is a dangerous habit when driving in work zones?

options.text: Not watching carefully for workers and moving equipment.

questions.explanation: In a work zone, slow down for traffic conditions and keep distance from other vehicles. Watch carefully for workers and equipment.

questions.question: To see objects in your blind spot when changing lanes, you should check:

options.text: Over your left or right shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Over your left or right shoulder.
questions.explanation: Your mirrors cannot show your blind spots. Look over your shoulder to check the blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: What should you do to avoid losing traction on wet roads?
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed on wet roads to prevent hydroplaning and keep tires in good condition. If you lose control, take your foot off the gas, do not brake, stay in your lane, and let the vehicle slow down naturally.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Reserved parking for persons with disabilities.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reserved parking for persons with disabilities.
questions.explanation: This sign marks parking spaces reserved for vehicles with disability license plates, disabled veteran license plates, or disabled parking placards.

questions.question: What must you do at an intersection with a flashing yellow light?

options.text: Wait for the green light before going.

questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down and be careful. Watch for crossing traffic and pedestrians before proceeding.

questions.question: Your reaction time is slower after:
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reflexes and reaction time. It reduces your vision, makes you less alert, and weakens your judgment. As you drink more, your driving skills decrease and you cannot judge distances, speeds, or other vehicles correctly.

questions.question: As daylight fades, what should you use to help others see you?
questions.explanation: Turn on your low beams as daylight begins to fade. Only use high beams in open areas where no other drivers are present.

questions.question: If there is a deep puddle ahead on the road, you should:

options.text: Keep the posted speed to get through the water.
Shift into neutral while driving through the water.

questions.explanation: Avoid slippery areas like ice, wet leaves, oil, and deep puddles to prevent skidding. Dry, solid surfaces are safest for driving.

questions.question: What does this yellow sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns that traffic may merge into your lane ahead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You must stop for other traffic.
Traffic is entering from another road. Give extra space for drivers to merge safely.
Traffic is entering from another road. Keep right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic is entering from another road. Give extra space for drivers to merge safely.
questions.explanation: This sign alerts you that traffic may merge ahead. Check your sides and rear. If possible, move to another lane to give merging drivers a clear path.

questions.question: You can identify an aggressive driver by:

options.text: The number of passengers in their car.

questions.explanation: Watch other drivers while you drive. If you see an aggressive driver making sudden or unsafe lane changes, do not challenge them. The safest choice is to move out of their way.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Last turn before a toll road.

questions.explanation: Orange is the color for work zones. When you see orange signs, cones, or barrels, stay alert and be ready for unexpected conditions. This sign warns you that a flagger is ahead. You must follow their directions.

questions.question: Orange background signs warn about:
questions.explanation: Orange signs are used only for construction and maintenance warnings.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, it is safe to return to your lane if you:

options.text: Cannot see the vehicle directly to your right.
See the vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.
Have passed the other vehicle's front bumper.

questions.correctAnswerText: See the vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Before moving back to your lane after passing, make sure you have enough space. When you see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror, you have enough room to return to your lane.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road may be slippery when wet. Drive carefully on slippery roads.

questions.question: On a freeway, look farther ahead than on a city street:

options.text: Because it takes a quarter mile to stop your vehicle.

questions.explanation: On the freeway, be ready for traffic changes. Watch for signals from other drivers. Expect vehicles merging at on-ramps and be prepared for sudden road and traffic changes.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: You must come to a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: An octagonal sign always means stop. Come to a complete stop at the stop line. If there is no stop line, stop before the crosswalk. If there is no crosswalk, stop before the intersection where you can see oncoming traffic. Proceed only when it is safe.

questions.question: Blue traffic signs provide information about:
questions.explanation: Blue signs provide information about motorist services, such as rest areas, food, gas, or hospitals.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign is displayed on slow-moving vehicles.

questions.question: This sign indicates a:
questions.explanation: Yellow signs with black markings warn about upcoming hazards. Round signs warn only about railroad crossings.
